correctness.rationale: An exact marked Euler-product identity gives W(q)=qB′(q)-4B(q)L(q); mod2 Jacobi cubic and sigma parity identify the coefficient correction with two explicitly defined quadratic-form representation counts. Jacobi two-square formula and residue class 8n+1=1 mod8 imply R1=(sum chi4-1_square)/2. For p=5,7 mod8 odd valuation, -2 is nonsquare so R2=0. The mod8 product constraint forces two odd-exponent 5 mod8 primes when p=5, giving 4|sum chi4; p=7 kills sum chi4. Thus 2|R1, establishing the transfer for every n. Exact p-adic valuations equal one on all ten progressions; the cited b4 theorems finish the infinite congruences. Boundaries n=0, all positive t, and signed/axial square representations accounted for. Standalone independent DP and form enumeration match for 0<=n<=2400; bounded computations are supplementary.

value.rationale: The original weighted statistic was recently introduced and previously had a narrow modulo-four family. The new all-n modulo-eight quadratic-form reduction exposes two distinct norm obstructions; a prime-factor argument yields an infinite, arithmetic, easily checkable transfer condition at all 5/7 mod8 primes. It converts two independent strong b4 counting theorems into ten genuinely weighted Ramanujan-type progressions with explicit moduli. This is motivated structural progress, not arbitrary finite coefficient enumeration or a cosmetic restatement of known b4 congruences.
